segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ אֵין בֵּין שִׁילֹה לִירוּשָׁלַיִם, אֶלָּא שֶׁבְּשִׁילֹה אוֹכְלִין קָדָשִׁים קַלִּים וּמַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי בְּכׇל הָרוֹאֶה, וּבִירוּשָׁלַיִם לִפְנִים מִן הַחוֹמָה.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» «The difference between» the Tabernacle in «Shilo and» the Temple in «Jerusalem is only that in Shiloh one eats offerings of lesser sanctity,» e.g., individual peace-offerings, thanks-offerings, and the Paschal lamb, «and» also «the second tithe, in any place that overlooks» Shiloh, as Shiloh was not a walled city and any place within its Shabbat boundary was regarded as part of the city. «And in Jerusalem» one eats those consecrated items only «within the walls.»

segments.he: וְכָאן וְכָאן, קׇדְשֵׁי קֳדָשִׁים נֶאֱכָלִין לִפְנִים מִן הַקְּלָעִים. קְדוּשַּׁת שִׁילֹה —
segments.en: «And here,» in Shiloh, «and there,» in Jerusalem, «offerings of the most sacred order are eaten» only «within the hangings.» The Tabernacle courtyard in Shiloh was surrounded by hangings and the Temple courtyard in Jerusalem was surrounded by a wall. There is another difference: With regard to «the sanctity of Shiloh,»

segments.he: יֵשׁ אַחֲרֶיהָ הֶיתֵּר, וּקְדוּשַּׁת יְרוּשָׁלַיִם — אֵין אַחֲרֶיהָ הֶיתֵּר.
segments.en: «after» the Tabernacle was destroyed, «there is permission» to sacrifice offerings on improvised altars. «But» with regard to «the sanctity of Jerusalem, after» the Temple was destroyed, «there is no permission» to sacrifice offerings on improvised altars, as the prohibition remains intact.

moves.summary: lesser offerings and second tithe: anywhere in view of Shiloh vs within Jerusalem's walls
most sacred offerings in both eaten within the hangings
after Shiloh, bamot permitted; after Jerusalem, not

positions.claim: Shiloh's sanctity lapsed after its destruction; Jerusalem's did not
